name: 160 Meters
blurb: The 'Top Band'. Strong ground-wave and night-time skywave propagation; popular for regional nets after sunset.

name: 80 Meters
blurb: Reliable night-time regional coverage; a common choice for local and emergency traffic nets.

name: 40 Meters
blurb: Workhorse band, day and night propagation; heavily used for digital modes like FT8.

name: 30 Meters
blurb: A WARC band reserved for CW and narrowband digital modes; no phone/SSB permitted.

name: 20 Meters
blurb: The classic DX band; strong daytime long-distance propagation across continents.

name: 17 Meters
blurb: A WARC band with 20m-like propagation but much lighter traffic.

name: 15 Meters
blurb: Excellent daytime DX during high solar activity; quieter during solar minimum.

name: 12 Meters
blurb: A narrow WARC band that opens well during favorable solar conditions.

name: 10 Meters
blurb: Can be dead or wide open; famous for sporadic-E openings and repeaters during solar maximum.

name: 6 Meters
blurb: Blends HF and VHF behavior; famous unpredictable long-distance openings.

name: 2 Meters
typicalModes: FM, SSB, DMR, D-STAR, C4FM, APRS
blurb: The primary local VHF band; most FM and digital voice repeaters live here.

name: 70 Centimeters
blurb: Dense UHF repeater coordination band, widely used for DMR and other digital voice systems.
